articles.title: Por que Fergie saiu dos Black Eyed Peas e quem canta com eles hoje?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Trio se apresenta no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro. Entenda por que a cantora não faz parte do grupo, apesar de encontros recentes, e quem é a vocalista atual.
articles.summary: Trio se apresenta no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro. Entenda por que a cantora não faz parte do grupo, apesar de encontros recentes, e quem é a vocalista atual.
articles.body:
Os Black Eyed Peas se apresentam no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Essa é a segunda vez do grupo no festival: eles vieram em 2019, em show com participação de Anitta.

Na época da última vinda, os Black Eyed Peas já eram um trio, sem a presença de Fergie. Mas até hoje, a cantora é lembrada por ter feito parte dos hits mais icônicos da banda. Abaixo, relembre por que Fergie saiu do grupo e quem é a atual vocalista feminina do Black Eyed Peas:

Por que Fergie saiu dos Black Eyed Peas?

Os Black Eyed Peas foram formados nos anos 90 como um trio. Fergie entrou no grupo em 2002, durante a produção do disco "Elephunk" e, a partir daí, o grupo atingiu seu auge comercial.

Com Fergie, discos como "Monkey Business", "The E.N.D." e "The Beginning" tiveram vários hits e colocaram o grupo no topo das paradas. Isso até 2011, quando o grupo anunciou que iria dar uma pausa por tempo indeterminado.

Os Black Eyed Peas voltaram em 2015, com singles lançados já sem a participação de Fergie. Até então, dizia-se que era só uma pausa para a vocalista focar no seu segundo álbum solo, "Double Dutchess".

Sua saída foi oficializada só em 2017, por Will.i.Am, que reforçou que a cantora não seria substituída . Segundo os integrantes, não foi um rompimento hostil.

Anos mais tarde, Taboo disse que, naquela época, Fergie saiu porque queria se dedicar integralmente à maternidade.

Recentemente, os quatro voltaram a aparecer juntos. Em uma entrevista com o produtor brasileiro Papatinho, veiculada em janeiro deste ano, Will.I.Am revelou que "o sonho dele" era fazer um disco do Black Eyed Peas para o Carnaval do Rio.

"Imagina se o Black Eyed Peas fizer um álbum sobre o Carnaval do Rio e no Carnaval do Rio. E sou eu, Taboo, Apl e Fergie. Isso seria épico. Se a gente fosse trazer essa formação de volta, isso precisa acontecer no Brasil, no Carnaval. Esse é o palco para isso", disse.

Em maio, o grupo foi como um quarteto para receber um prêmio nos American Music Awards. Apesar disso, não há confirmação de que ela vai voltar para o grupo.

Will.i.Am fez o possível para cumprir sua promessa de não substituir Fergie. Hoje, os Black Eyed Peas são oficialmente um trio, mas contam com a ajuda de vocais femininos para os maiores hits. Afinal, faixas como "Meet Me Halfway" ou "Boom Boom Pow" não seriam as mesmas sem os trechos da cantora.

Atualmente, quem costuma fazer essa parte é a cantora filipina J. Rey Soul .

J. Rey Soul é a atual cantora do Black Eyed Peas — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook

Às vezes, o grupo também convida cantores de algumas parcerias, como aconteceu com Anitta no Rock in Rio de 2019. Juntos, eles lançaram a canção "Explosion".

articles.title: Lionel Richie segue na UTI para investigar problema cardíaco | G1
articles.standfirst: Lionel Richie foi internado após passar mal no fim de uma apresentação em St. Louis. Cantor tem previsão de alta para quarta-feira (3).
articles.summary: Lionel Richie segue internado em uma UTI nos EUA para exames cardíacos após passar mal em show, com previsão de alta para esta quarta-feira (3).
articles.body:
Lionel Richie durante apresentação no show de coroação do Rei Charles III, em Londres, em 7 de maio de 2023 — Foto: Chris Jackson/Pool via Reuters

Lionel Richie, de 77 anos, segue internado na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) após passar mal durante um show nos EUA. Segundo o site TMZ, o cantor passa por uma bateria de exames por conta de problemas cardíacos.

Segundo o TMZ, após dar entrada em um hospital local para realizar exames, os médicos investigam uma possível desidratação e a previsão era de alta nesta terça-feira (2).

No entanto, os médicos decidiram investigar como estava o coração do cantor. A previsão de alta foi alterada para esta quarta-feira (3).

Testemunhas que estavam no show relataram ao TMZ que Lionel aparentou ter dificuldades no fim da apresentação. Durante a última música, "All Night Long", ele pediu à equipe que levasse uma cadeira ao palco para que pudesse se sentar enquanto cantava.

Em junho, o cantor passou por outro susto. Após passar mal em um show na cidade de Saint Paul, ele foi levado às pressas para um hospital.

No dia, ele disse à plateia que estava "tonto" e "estranho".

Lionel Richie, nascido em 1949 no Alabama, é um dos maiores nomes do pop e do soul dos Estados Unidos. Ficou famoso nos anos 1970 como vocalista dos Commodores e depois seguiu carreira solo. Vendeu mais de 90 milhões de discos e ganhou quatro Grammys.

Entre os seus maiores hits estão "All Night Long (All Night)", "Hello" e "Say You, Say Me". Foi com esta última, tema do filme "O Sol da Meia-Noite", que Richie levou o Oscar de melhor canção original, em 1986. Ele também é jurado do programa "American Idol".

articles.title: Twenty One Pilots, eles cresceram: como dupla virou um dos maiores nomes do rock após três Lollas | G1
articles.standfirst: Banda encerra o Rock in Rio no dia 13 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Baterista já explicou ao g1 por que é difícil perceber a própria evolução.
articles.summary: Banda encerra o Rock in Rio no dia 13 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Baterista já explicou ao g1 por que é difícil perceber a própria evolução.
articles.body:
A trajetória do Twenty One Pilots no Brasil ajuda a entender não apenas a evolução técnica de Tyler Joseph e Josh Dun, mas como a próprio pop rock mudou nos últimos dez anos. A recusa de rótulos e o trânsito livre por estilos unem as maiores novidades recentes do rock.

Quando pisaram pela primeira vez no palco do Lollapalooza, em 2016, eles eram vistos por parte do público como uma curiosidade: uma dupla com pose de youtubers mascarados, mistura afiada de rap com indie e uma energia que compensava a escassez de instrumentos com o uso de bases pré-gravadas e acrobacias.

Twenty One Pilots se apresentam no palco Skol do Lollapalooza 2016 — Foto: Flavio Moraes/G1

Naquela estreia, faixas como "Stressed Out" e "Car Radio" já mostravam o apelo direto com a fatia mais jovem da plateia. Era um som moldado por dilemas existenciais, letras com tom positivo e uma salada de influências que ia do hip hop ao poperô. Em entrevista ao g1 na época , Josh Dun justificava a formação enxuta e a mistura estilística: "A gente notou que tocava melhor assim. Mas ao mesmo tempo, nos sentimos vulneráveis com só dois no palco". A vulnerabilidade virou combustível.

Três anos depois, no Lollapalooza 2019, o cenário era outro. A dupla desembarcou no Autódromo de Interlagos carregando a era "Trench", que pintou a plateia de preto e amarelo com fitas, lenços e cabelos tingidos . Maior, o duo foi eleito o melhor show daquela edição, entregando um caos sonoro e performático que reforçava a tese de "gênero fluido" defendida por Josh Dun antes de subir ao palco: "Não sei se o que tocamos é rock, e isso não importa".

A escalada do grupo não se restringiu às edições do festival paulistano. Em novembro de 2022, o Twenty One Pilots dividiu o protagonismo do GPWeek com o The Killers, tocando para 50 mil pessoas em São Paulo. No estádio do Palmeiras, Tyler e Josh provaram que já sabiam conduzir multidões. Ali começou a ficar evidente o amadurecimento musical, com arranjos mais dançantes (como o groove de "The Outside") e o apoio de uma banda no fundo, sem abrir mão do habitual show de luzes de celulares e da clássica escalada nas estruturas de iluminação.

Twenty One Pilots se apresenta no Lollapalooza 2023 — Foto: Rafael Leal/g1

A consagração em Interlagos veio em 2023, quando foram escalados de última hora para substituir o Blink-182. A dupla não estava sozinha em cena: baixista, tecladista, guitarrista e trompetista encorparam o som com R&B e disco music. O setlist ganhou até tributos brasileiros, como os versos de bossa nova e funk puxados pelos metais. Tyler manteve o ritual de escalar a estrutura de iluminação durante "Car Radio", mas o brilho veio nos arranjos que provaram o salto de patamar.

A caminhada iniciada lá em 2016 ganha um novo capítulo no dia 13 de setembro. Escalados para fechar o Rock in Rio, Tyler Joseph e Josh Dun chegam à Cidade do Rock não mais como uma aposta barulhenta ou uma aposta adolescente, mas como headliners consolidados. A dupla que começou se sentindo vulnerável com apenas dois integrantes no palco prova que a falta de fronteiras nos gêneros musicais foi o caminho mais direto para o topo do rock atual.

articles.title: Akshay Kumar, Ranbir Kapoor, Kartik Aaryan came forward to help veteran Sudhir Dalvi of 'Sai Baba' fame after hospital bill went to Rs 19 lakh, wife says he's now recovering at home
articles.summary: Veteran actor Sudhir Dalvi, widely remembered for his iconic portrayal of Sai Baba in the 1977 film Shirdi Ke Sai Baba, is slowly recovering at home f.
articles.body: Veteran actor Sudhir Dalvi, widely remembered for his iconic portrayal of Sai Baba in the 1977 film Shirdi Ke Sai Baba, is slowly recovering at home following a serious health setback. The 86-year-old actor spent nearly a month at Mumbai’s Lilavati Hospital after being admitted on October 7, 2025, with sepsis, a potentially life-threatening infection that affects the bloodstream.The prolonged illness affected his joints and significantly restricted the movement of his limbs, eventually requiring treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). During his hospitalisation, the rising medical costs reportedly became a major concern for his family.According to an NDTV report, Sudhir Dalvi’s hospital expenses had crossed Rs 19 lakh, while doctors estimated that the overall treatment costs could climb further. With the family finding it increasingly difficult to manage the bills, assistance came from several quarters.In December 2025, the Bombay High Court permitted the Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust to contribute Rs 11 lakh towards the actor’s medical treatment. Several members of the film fraternity also stepped forward financially, with Kartik Aaryan, Ranbir Kapoor and Akshay Kumar among those who extended support.Speaking about the difficult period, Sudhir’s wife Suhas Dalvi opened up about the financial strain caused by his hospitalisation. She also provided an update on his condition, revealing that the actor is now back home and able to walk with assistance. Bollyspice quoted her saying, "He is at home now. He still has to walk with the help of a walker, and his mind is disoriented. But he is happy to be home. So am I. The hospital was not only expensive, but the aura of being in a hospital is also very intimidating for a patient."Suhas also expressed gratitude towards the film industry and fans who rallied behind the family when news of their financial difficulties emerged. She said, "When the news spread that we were unable to meet hospital bills, many from the film industry came forward to help financially. I can’t immediately recall all the names. But Kartik Aaryan, Ranbir Kapoor, and Akshay Kumar were among the first to help. There were so many others from the film industry and outside. My husband is best known for playing Sai Baba. So many Sai bhakts came forward to help. Who says we’ve become a heartless people? The love and generosity after my husband’s illness is overwhelming."While the financial support helped the family navigate the actor’s treatment, Suhas now believes that monetary assistance is no longer necessary. Instead, she has appealed for prayers as Sudhir continues his slow recovery.She said, "In fact, we request the film association, which is so kindly sending money every month, to use that money for someone needier. My husband has received all the medical help he could get. Now it is just prayers that he needs. His recovery is slow. I am myself old and asthmatic. But I am doing my best to look after both of us."For now, the veteran actor remains at home and continues his recovery with support from his family. articles.title: Meet Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's new dog. She's already a model.
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s dog stepped into the spotlight with a starring role in Kelce’s new Tommy Hilfiger campaign.
articles.body:
There's a new addition to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's family. The famous couple's white, fluffy Samoyed pup made her public debut in a new ad campaign.

The dog, rumored to be named Wendy, was first spotted earlier this summer when she stepped off a plane in Palm Springs with her Kansas City Chiefs tight end father and Grammy-winning mom. Alas, the world received no formal introduction to the pup — until Tuesday, when she appeared in a Tommy Hilfiger ad campaign alongside Kelce. The new ad shows Kelce checking into the Plaza Hotel with one very good girl by his side.

In an interview with Vogue about the campaign, which also features stars like Swift's bestie Gigi Hadid, Kelce said that their pup "lights up my day." So, naturally, when Tommy Hilfiger was seeking a dog to accompany Kelce in the campaign, the nepo puppy was the ideal choice.

"We figured, why not her? She crushed it and actually really fit into that Tommy aesthetic too," he told the magazine. "Those are some of my favorite shots."

The Samoyed may have been part of Kelce and Swift's lives for quite a while. In February 2025, Kelce's brother Jason Kelce revealed that the Happy Gilmore 2 actor had a new puppy — who ate the back of Kelce's velvet couch — on the Fitz & Whit podcast.

Swift, who wed Kelce at Madison Square Garden on July 3 after nearly three years of dating, has not had a dog of her own. The self-proclaimed "childless cat lady" has three cats — Olivia Benson, Meredith Grey and Benjamin Button — who often appear in her music videos and social media posts.

Despite being a cat person, Swift does have a dog sibling : Her mother Andrea Swift has a massive Great Dane — ironically named Kitty . In fact, Swift named a character in her song "The Life of a Showgirl" after Kitty .

articles.title: Ram Gopal Varma reacts to Allu Aravind's comment on Yash, says 'only highly egotistic people will take his statement personally', fans hit back at the 'Satya' maker
articles.summary: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has stepped into the controversy surrounding producer Allu Aravind’s recent remark about Yash, coming to the latter’s defenc.
articles.body: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has stepped into the controversy surrounding producer Allu Aravind’s recent remark about Yash, coming to the latter’s defence while arguing that the statement has been taken out of context.Allu Aravind had sparked a debate with his “Who was Yash before KGF?” comment. Reacting to the backlash, Varma described the controversy as “ridiculously laughable” and attempted to explain the context in which he believed the producer made the remark.Ram Gopal Varma wrote on X, “The controversy regarding #AlluAravind ‘s statement regarding #Yash is ridiculously laughable because what he clearly meant when he talked about big films with unknown actors and saying he dint know of Yash before KGF , even a dumbo should understand that it was in context of the below. The Hindi audience dint know Prabhas before Bahubali , they dint know Rishab before Kantara , I dint know Brando before Godfather..Maybe he was a star before in his films A street car named desire , on the water front etc ..I don’t know if they released in india also .. That’s because those films made them big stars and not the other way around ..Hollywood always spends big on concept films and not on stars ..Even directors like Nolan use names only for their acting prowess and not to depend on their stardom ..We all know whether it’s Oppenheimer or Odyssey , they would work as much irrespective of who’s in it."Varma argued that an actor’s popularity can change dramatically when a film reaches a much wider audience. Drawing parallels from Indian cinema, he pointed to Prabhas’ transformation into a pan-India star following Baahubali and Rishab Shetty’s increased recognition after Kantara. He also cited Hollywood icon Marlon Brando to illustrate how an actor can be established in one space but become significantly more recognised after appearing in a widely successful film.Varma then criticised those who interpreted Allu Aravind’s statement as a personal attack on Yash, suggesting that such reactions were driven by ego.“It’s only highly egotistic people who will take his statement personally on such a general well meaning thought ..Actually this kind of reaction also explains why they are making what they are making.”However, Varma’s intervention itself soon became a topic of discussion online. Some social media users interpreted his comments as another indirect dig at Yash rather than simply a defence of Allu Aravind.One user questioned, “You have been attacking Yash nonstop but he is not reacting to you, why?”Another asked, “Did Yash reject any of your scripts?”The exchange comes amid growing discussion around Yash’s journey from being a regional star to becoming a major pan-India name following the success of the KGF franchise.This statement also came amid the release of 'Toxic'. articles.title: Trump & Melania’s Marriage Reportedly ‘Not in a Healthy Place’ After Report She’s ‘Obsessed’ with His Aide—They ‘Barely Speak’
articles.summary: Will they ever work things out?
articles.body:
High-profile celebrity couples are frequently confronted with split rumors, and one pair that's faced such speculation for years is President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump .

Reports indicate they don't get along and even sleep in separate rooms, with new claims from The Irish Star suggesting that their marriage is barely hanging on by a thread.

According to the outlet, Trump's executive assistant, Natalie Harp , is partially to blame for the POTUS' strained relationship with Melania. Harp is reportedly "obsessed" with Trump and has been seen with him far more than Melania, who, according to The Daily Beast , has only been seen in public 38 days in 2026.

Trump biographer Michael Wolff previously alleged on his Substack that Melania's locked in a power struggle with Harp and "would not show up" to events if Harp was in attendance. Wolff also claimed that Trump and Melania "barely speak" these days.

In response, relationship expert Gemma Logan told The Irish Star that their marriage is likely "not in a healthy place."

"A marriage where two people are reportedly barely speaking is clearly not in a healthy place. Communication is the heartbeat of any long term relationship," she said. "When conversation becomes minimal, couples can start living parallel lives rather than a shared one. At that point, the question isn't simply whether they spend time together, but whether they still feel emotionally connected when they do."

Despite an alleged rough patch, Logan believes the two could eventually come back stronger than ever. "If reports about Donald and Melania Trump are accurate, the most important thing to remember is that distance in a marriage doesn't always mean the relationship is over."

"Some couples need constant closeness to feel connected," she continued. "Others function with far more independence, particularly when both partners have demanding lives, strong personalities and very different ways of dealing with public attention."

Logan even pointed out that there's a good chance a marriage "can survive distance"—as long as there isn't an "emotional disconnection" between both parties. "Living in different places doesn't automatically spell trouble. Plenty of couples have successful relationships while spending significant periods apart because of work, family responsibilities or lifestyle choices."

"The real issue is what happens emotionally during that time," she noted. "If the distance is mutually agreed, openly discussed and balanced with genuine affection, it can work. In some cases, a little breathing room can even make a relationship stronger."

Logan added, "However, if physical distance is being used to avoid conflict, emotional intimacy or difficult conversations, it can become a sign of a much deeper problem. The key question for Donald and Melania Trump is whether their separate routines are simply practical or whether they reflect a relationship that has become increasingly separate in every meaningful sense."

Even though Wolff alleged Melania has major issues with Harp, Hollywood insider Rob Shuter reported otherwise. Sources told Shuter that Melania is actually "relieved" that someone else is willing to be by Trump's side 24/7.

"Melania isn't jealous of Natalie — she's grateful for her," a Trumpworld source told Naughty But Nice . "Donald demands constant attention, and Natalie genuinely seems to enjoy giving it to him. For Melania, that takes an enormous amount of pressure off."

Another insider went on to say that Harp "wants to be there for every meeting, every trip, every moment," while Melania would rather skip it all. "They want entirely different relationships with Donald, and that's exactly why this works."

"Melania hates becoming part of somebody else's gossip, but she absolutely doesn't want Natalie gone," a separate source stated. "Why would she? Natalie handles the exhausting, around-the-clock Donald duty Melania has spent years avoiding."

articles.title: Luke Bryan threatens to 'knock the s--- out of' online trolls trashing his new song
articles.summary: Luke Bryan told Theo Von he'd confront trolls who accused his "Fish Hunt Golf Drink" song of being AI-generated, calling out teenage critics online.
articles.body: Luke Bryan has a bone to pick with his haters. During an appearance on the "This Past Weekend with Theo Von" podcast, the "American Idol" judge and country star opened up about the backlash surrounding his latest song, "Fish Hunt Golf Drink," which some social media users accused of being created with artificial intelligence. And now, whether you like the song or not, or whether you like me as an artist, whether you like what I'm about or whatever … now I'm the guy that somebody said that I AI-ed a song and wrote it. articles.title: Fontaines D.C. singer in Cwmbran Celtic FC shirt at Reading Festival
articles.summary: The club says sales of the shirt almost doubled after it was worn by Fontaines D.C frontman Grian Chatten.
articles.body:
A semi-professional Welsh football club say they were "in shock" after their shirt was worn during a Reading Festival headline set.

Fontaines D.C. frontman Grian Chatten was seen sporting a green and white-striped Cwmbran Celtic away shirt during the performance on Friday, leading to pre-sales of the shirt to "almost double".

In a post shared on social media, the club said "we're still in shock and can't thank Grian enough for the support".

Sales of the shirt go both towards supporting the club as well as to grassroots music venues, with the club having partnered with four famous bands for their 2026/27 season team kits .

They include Welsh groups Super Furry Animals and Panic Shack, as well as Loose Articles and Mogwai, with the latter appearing as a sponsor on the shirt worn by Chatten at Reading.

Chatten said in a statement to BBC Wales: "I love Cwmbran and I love initiatives that support independent venues.

"Cwmbran Celtic is a club run by volunteers who have a sense of solidarity with the plight independent music venues are facing. I think that's class. Also I love Mogwai."

Matt Jarrett, joint commercial manager for the club, said they "never expected a totally different band, who weren't on the shirt to end up wearing it on stage".

He said a friend of the club worked as the monitor engineer for Fontaines D.C., and helped get a size 3XL to Chatten.

"In all honesty, we thought we'll give it to him. It'll be nice for him to have it. Maybe he will wear it backstage or something," said Jarrett.

But to the club and its supporters' surprise, Chatten not only wore the shirt but performed the bands headline set in it - in front of tens of thousands at the festival and many more online and on television.

"We were as surprised as anyone when we saw him walking out on stage with the shirt on," Jarrett said.

Jarrett said it had been "crazy" ever since, after festival-goers and viewers shared photos and videos of the band's performance.

"Our pre-sale orders have almost doubled from last Friday," he said.

"The Fontaines fans have gone crazy over it."

Jarrett, who also owns a record store in Newport, said 10% of shirt sale profits would go to the Music Venues Trust.

articles.title: Google needs Hollywood more than the studios need AI
articles.summary: Google has everything to gain from striking licensing deals with movie studios, but the entertainment industry has to be careful about how it embraces AI.
articles.body: Google has reportedly been reaching out to a number of Hollywood’s biggest studios, hoping to strike licensing agreements that would allow it to train its AI models on copyrighted material in exchange for massive piles of cash. In theory, these deals would be a win-win: a huge financial boon to the studios that would also give Google a significant advantage in its race to outpace other AI companies. But while there’s little downside for Google, these deals pose a distinct set of risks to each of the studios that might be thinking about going all-in on AI. Getting into bed with Google this way might benefit Hollywood in the short term, but it could just as easily backfire and leave the public feeling burned by the entertainment industry. Though Google has not yet been able to get Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, or Universal to agree to anything officially, the company’s executives have been reaching out to multiple studio representatives with pitches focused on its AI technology, according to unnamed sources speaking to The Los Angeles Times. Google wants permission to train its AI models on the studios’ vast libraries of copyrighted content, and it’s willing to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to get ahold of them. Per The LA Times, Google could pay a studio like Disney / Pixar around $40 million just for the rights to generate outputs featuring a single copyrighted character. That payout could swell well into the billions the more characters Google’s deals encompass, and studios might be able to secure a portion of however much advertising revenue Google makes from AI-generated content featuring that IP on platforms like YouTube. As expensive as these partnerships would be for Google, they would also be an invaluable tool as the company continues to crystalize its position as one of the most prominent players in the AI game. Gemini being able to spit out Disney-approved images of Darth Vader and Snow White might not seem all that significant on its face, but that’s exactly the sort of thing that could get more ordinary, non tech-obsessed people seeing generative AI in a more positive (if innocuous) light. After years of hearing AI companies boast about their plans to disrupt society and eliminate jobs, public sentiment — especially among young people — about the technology has shifted into the negative. Even with tools like ChatGPT being as popular as they are, the larger AI industry has been so mired in controversy and plagued by concerns about its real world harms that it would now be hard-pressed to put out products that would immediately curry widespread goodwill. Striking deals with film and TV studios would give Google a convenient way to shift the larger narrative about its AI ambitions. The content developed through these partnerships would presumably look better than the slop currently being churned out by models trained on ill-gotten source data, and having Google’s name and logos slapped all over official AI-generated Disney content would do wonders to legitimize this technology in people’s minds. But even if it didn’t, the partnership would still signal to the public that the entertainment industry sees generative AI as a tool worth embracing. It’s hard to quantify how valuable that framing would be to Google, whose DeepMind arm struck a $75 million investment deal with A24 earlier this summer. But it’s very easy to imagine how taking Google’s AI cash could put studios on a path that ultimately alienates their workers and audiences. Regardless of whether a studio were to incorporate AI tools into their production workflows or simply feature user-generated AI content on their platforms (which was Disney and OpenAI’s plan before their partnership collapsed), striking a licensing agreement with Google would be a watershed moment. Lionsgate, a notable studio but not a major player, struck a licensing deal with Runway in 2024. So far, nothing concrete has come out of that partnership, but the companies say they’re working on a plan to release AI-generated shorts. Once any one of the big legacy studios hop on to the AI bandwagon and manage to actually make something they can show the world, more production houses have a reason to follow suit. AI’s potential to speed production timelines up while keeping costs down is one of the main things that has kept studios interested in utilizing the technology. Shareholders would absolutely love it if production houses could put out more movies while spending less money, but doing that by using AI tools would almost certainly put a significant portion of the entertainment workforce out of jobs. What may be keeping Disney and other studios from rushing to take Google up on its offers is the way that people have reacted to seeing AI used in the production of films like Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Fans were dismayed to find AI-generated images in Brand New Day’s official artbook, and the negative reaction might have been even more intense had people known about the technology’s use before the film hit theaters. It’s impossible to know for sure whether awareness about AI’s presence in Brand New Day’s production would have kept it from making $2 billion at the box office. But it stands to reason that none of the studios is eager to be the first to learn what happens when they release a project that’s presented as being the product of Google’s AI tools. Though Google has everything to gain from Hollywood embracing AI, the studios have to be mindful of how endorsing this technology could leave them out on a limb. And as much as Google might be presenting its products as the solution to all of the entertainment industry’s issues, the AI industry needs Hollywood more than Hollywood needs more slop.

articles.title: Thea Frodin, who depicted Serena Williams as ‘King Richard’ body double, makes US Open debut
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Five years ago, Thea Frodin depicted Serena Williams in the Oscar-winning movie “King Richard,” performing as a body double. In a full-circle mome...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Five years ago, Thea Frodin depicted Serena Williams in the Oscar-winning movie "King Richard," performing as a body double.

In a full-circle moment Tuesday afternoon, Frodin competed in a tournament that Williams long dominated.

Frodin, 17, made her WTA Tour debut in the first round of the US Open, losing to second-seeded Elena Rybakina 6-3, 6-2 at the Grandstand stadium.

Despite the final outcome, the California-born Frodin held her own in front of a supportive American crowd, ripping 11 aces and taking five games against the reigning Australian Open champion.

"I tried going out there to see what it would be like just to feel no pressure," Frodin said. "Yeah, just go out there and have a fun time. I feel like that's what I accomplished, and obviously I have a lot to learn, but I'm excited with most of the things I did out there."

A soon-to-be high school senior, Frodin earned a wild-card entry at the US Open by winning the USTA Billie Jean King Girls' 18s National Championships.

But long before then, Frodin cemented her place in mainstream culture by serving as the body double to actress Demi Singleton, who played a young Serena in the 2021 sports biopic about the Williams sisters' upbringing by their eccentric father, Richard Williams.

Will Smith starred as the title character and won Best Actor at the Academy Awards for his portrayal.

Frodin said she had not yet met Serena, who was an executive producer on the film. Serena — a six-time singles champion at the US Open — is set to compete with her sister Venus Williams in the doubles tournament at Flushing Meadows this week.

"Hopefully I can get the chance soon, to get the opportunity to meet her," said Frodin, who is No. 585 in the world rankings.

Frodin commanded more fanfare than the typical wild-card participant due to her Hollywood history. While Frodin certainly noticed the attention, she said it did not affect her.

"I think it's hard to get away from all of that," Frodin said. "It's kind of just about accepting it and not letting it get to you. I feel like I did a good job of that. Obviously, I saw that Will Smith reposted one of my posts, so that was pretty cool."

The Kazakhstan-born Rybakina said her team informed her of Frodin's unique backstory. She came away impressed by the teenager.

"I didn't see the movie," Rybakina, 27, said. "But yeah, it's a cool experience, definitely."

articles.title: De Adele a Beyoncé: Quais artistas o Rock in Rio ainda sonha em levar para o festival?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Vice-presidente Artístico da Rock World, Zé Ricardo fala sobre torcida por ter cantora inglesa e Paul McCartney nos palcos do evento. Ele também quer retorno de Beyoncé e Rihanna.
articles.summary: Vice-presidente Artístico da Rock World, Zé Ricardo fala sobre torcida por ter cantora inglesa e Paul McCartney nos palcos do evento. Ele também quer retorno de Beyoncé e Rihanna.
articles.body:
Quem são as estrelas que o Rock in Rio ainda sonha em trazer para o festival? Apesar de já ter levado milhares de artistas para seus palcos ao longo dos anos, o festival ainda tem sua lista de desejos. Seja para estreias ou para retorno.

"É tanta gente. Adele, Beyoncé, Rihanna... Tem muita gente. Mas pelo menos esse top 3 aí, são artistas que a gente tem muita vontade de trazer, que a gente batalha muito e que também querem tocar no festival, mas que precisa de muita logística", afirma Zé Ricardo, vice-presidente Artístico da Rock World (empresa que criou, organiza e produz o Rock in Rio e o The Town).

Beyoncé e Rihanna não seriam apresentações inéditas no festival, já que a primeira esteve no evento em 2013, enquanto a segunda, subiu ao palco do festival de 2015.

"Adele falta ainda. Mas Adele não sei se ela quer", diz Zé, que ainda sonha com a presença de Paul McCartney.

Adele, Paul McCartney, Beyoncé e Rihanna estão na lista dos sonhos do Rock in Rio para se apresentar no festival — Foto: Reuters/AFP

"É um cara que a gente sempre sonhou trazer e que sempre fica perto por dias, por meses. A gente já fez com ele em Lisboa, mas no Brasil ainda não."

O cantor britânico esteve no festival português em 2004.

Ao falar sobre a curadoria o festival, Zé Ricardo explica que ela é feita "cirurgicamente" e que tudo "tem uma narrativa e uma mensagem subliminar por trás".

"Às vezes a gente consegue chegar no objetivo, às vezes a gente fica perto, às vezes a gente tenta. Mas a ideia é sempre propor."

"Então estou propondo coisas para que o público que venha para o Rock in Rio saia com uma coisa que eles não tinham antes. Isso é muito importante. Se você comprar um ingresso e sair daqui com a mesma coisa que você tinha, meu trabalho foi ruim."

Em 2026, um desses planejamentos de palco que soma o fator proposta com a engenharia cirúrgica na curadoria envolve o dia 11 de setembro.

Nesta data, os headliners dos palcos Mundo e Sunset, respectivamente, são Stray Kids e Jamiroquai. Apesar de curiosa, a escolha de artistas de gêneros tão diferentes não foi por acaso.

E envolve dois pontos. O primeiro, é sobre uma proposta de trazer experiências diferentes nos dois palcos principais do festival.

Sexto dia de Rock in Rio — Foto: Thaís Espírito Santo/g1

"Nesse dia, o Sunset é construído para ter um tipo de diálogo dedicado a Soul Music. E, o Palco Mundo, para ter um diálogo mais voltado para o K-pop. E ainda com a presença do Alok, que é um artista que encanta qualquer tipo de público. Ele aproxima", explica Zé.

O segundo ponto envolve o fator "família". E veio com aprendizado de outra edição: a de 2024, quando o Rock in Rio trouxe Travis Scott.

"Quando eu fiz uma noite só de trap, os pais sofreram um pouco realmente. Eles ficaram sem um porto seguro. Aí eu repeti o Travis Scott no The Town por conta da imensa demanda que ele teve. E aí coloquei a Lauryn Hill no The One, foi uma alegria."

"Os pais deixavam de falar: 'Pô, vou ter que levar meu filho para ver o Travis' e falavam: 'E aí, filho, não quer ir ver o Travis, eu quero ver a Lauryn Hill'."

"Então, esse diálogo também existe. A gente sempre tenta trazer coisas que possam abraçar. Principalmente quando a gente tá falando com um time adolescente."

articles.summary: Cantora vai completar 20 apresentações em edições do festival realizadas no Brasil, Portugal, Espanha e Estados Unidos.
articles.body:
Ivete Sangalo em uma de suas participações no Rock in Rio — Foto: Marcelo Brnadt/G1

Nenhuma outra artista subiu tanto ao palco do Rock in Rio quanto Ivete Sangalo . A baiana lidera com folga a lista de nomes que mais vezes se apresentaram no festival. Em 2026, ela chegará à marca de 20 shows, somando participações nas edições realizadas em Portugal, Espanha, Estados Unidos e, claro, no Brasil.

A primeira participação aconteceu em 2004, na edição inaugural do Rock in Rio Lisboa. Desde então, a cantora se tornou uma presença constante no evento. Foi apenas em 2011, porém, que Ivete subiu ao palco da versão brasileira do festival pela primeira vez.

Ela já tinha cinco apresentações no festival (quatro em Lisboa e uma em Madri) na sua estreia no Brasil. Quando o nome de Ivete Sangalo foi anunciado no Rock in Rio, muitos reclamaram da escolha e batizaram o festival de "Axé in Rio" . Isso, porém, não a desanimou. Na época, Ivete afirmou que os roqueiros estenderam um tapete vermelho para ela se apresentar e por isso ela resolveu retribuir no palco.

"Nada mais justo que fazer um carinho a essas pessoas. Todo carinho reverte em carinho. É um dever nosso perpetuar as boas energias. Eu fiz um carinho para o público do rock, que me acolheu muito bem. 'More than words', do Extreme, eu decidi tocar no palco. Foi na hora".

Ivete Sangalo 'sobrevoa' show no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Stephanie Rodrigues/g1

Em 2022, Ivete voltou a ser alvo de críticas por sua presença constante no line-up do festival. Em entrevista ao jornal O Globo naquele ano, a diretora artística nacional do Palco Mundo, Marisa Menezes, saiu em defesa da cantora ao explicar sua importância para o evento.

"Ela nos salvou quando a Ariana Grande perdeu a voz e cancelou o show. Usou sua popularidade em Portugal e todo o seu carisma e habilidade para entreter um público que, originalmente, não tinha ido lá para vê-la. Ela é da família para sempre”, disse

A declaração faz referência ao Rock in Rio Lisboa de 2016, quando Ivete Sangalo substituiu Ariana Grande após a cantora americana cancelar sua apresentação devido a uma infecção na garganta.

Ao longo das participações, a baiana já levou tombo, anunciou o sexo de suas filhas gêmeas no palco , voou sobre a plateia e fez um dueto com Shakira. Este ano, ela retorna ao Rock in Rio, depois de rodar o país com a turnê “Ivete Clareou”, projeto dedicado ao samba e ao pagode.

articles.title: Diogo Defante: do Repórter Doidão ao palco do Rock in Rio como cantor | G1
articles.standfirst: Ele prepara show com robôs e figurinos futuristas. Ao g1, comenta a retirada de um tumor, o sucesso do Repórter Doidão e o período em que trabalhou com Felipe Neto.
articles.summary: Diogo Defante, o Repórter Doidão, detalha sua transição para a música, a superação de um tumor e os preparativos para o show com robôs no Rock in Rio.
articles.body:
Diogo Defante durante apresentação. — Foto: Reprodução/@fredinhonml.jpg

A música apareceu na vida de Diogo Defante muito antes do humor.

Aos 13 anos, o menino de Realengo (RJ) aprendeu a tocar bateria por conta própria. Orgulhoso de si mesmo e animado com a ideia de "se sentir vivo em cima de um palco", ele formou a banda "Let’s Go" com um grupinho de amigos.

Juntos, eles tocaram covers de clássicos do rock em vários aniversários por aí, ainda sem ganhar muito dinheiro, mas com a esperança de, em algum momento, conseguir se destacar na cena hardcore brasileira. A empreitada durou 9 anos. Não conseguiram.

Agora, aos 35 e já carregando nas costas a fama de ser o "Repórter Doidão" das entrevistas virais, Defante chega ao Rock in Rio para fechar o palco Supernova no dia 4 de setembro, por volta das 20h10.

O criador de conteúdo com mais de 5 milhões de seguidores (só no Instagram) confessa que só agora pôde, finalmente, se entregar a antiga paixão do jeito que gostaria: rendido pelo prazer, sem a obrigação do sucesso.

"Quando comecei a ter certa repercussão com comédia no YouTube, foi uma queda livre. Eu tinha que fazer aquelas pessoas rirem. A música é a minha válvula de escape, minha terapia. Eu é que quero me divertir", resumiu em entrevista ao g1.

Diogo Defante durante apresentação. — Foto: Divulgação/@rafaelstrabelli.jpg

Em 2023, Defante lançou o EP “Robson” e, no ano seguinte, apresentou o álbum “Tífane”, com oito faixas.

Agora, aproveitando o timing de sua apresentação no RIR, o artista dá continuidade à fase mais recente de sua carreira com “Humanoide”, faixa que aborda a relação entre seres humanos e inteligência artificial e que já ganhou clipe.

Seu som mistura rock, punk e referências do movimento contracultural manguebeat. Suas músicas lembram esquetes de humor, com letras que apostam no nonsense e no duplo sentido, como "Pelo" (2023), em que canta sobre pelos pubianos e depilação.

Um pentelho em desabafo Se queixou dos fundilhos anais Dos terríveis odores que ele atura A rosca ninguém raspa, só as partes frontais 🎶

Ele cita o grupo de humor Hermes e Renato e os Mamonas Assassinas entre suas principais referências. Em seu repertório, há ainda espaço para um cover de Perlla ("Tremendo Vacilão") e uma homenagem ao rei do brega, Reginaldo Rossi ("Garçom").

Ao g1 , ele relembra como a internet o afastou temporariamente da música, fala sobre o período em que trabalhou com Felipe Neto, revela como descobriu e retirou um tumor e detalha a preparação para o maior show de sua carreira. Confira:

g1 — A música é na verdade sua primeira paixão, e não o humor. Como se deu isso?

Diogo Defante — Comecei a tocar bateria aos 13 anos. Depois, a gente começou a fazer alguns shows e a banda foi tomando um rumo meio profissional. Eu era muito novo mas já estava preocupado com tudo: “Temos que gravar um álbum, como vamos fazer esse lançamento?”. Na época era Orkut, MySpace... Eu ficava no Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V: “Maria, José, ouve aí meu som”. Fazia essa divulgação braçal e conseguia converter umas dez pessoas para ir ao show cantar nossas músicas.

g1 — E vocês chegaram a viver da música em algum momento?

Defante — A gente chegou a morar em São Paulo por um ano e meio. Mas ganhar dinheiro mesmo era muito difícil. O autoral é muito ingrato nesse sentido. A oportunidade que a gente tinha era abrir shows de bandas grandes, mas não tinha produtor que pagasse para uma banda autoral desconhecida que não vendia ingresso como a gente.

Diogo Defante durante apresentação. — Foto: Divulgação/@nandaariasfotografia

g1 — Por causa disso você resolveu apostar na internet?

Defante — Eu peguei uma outra estrada artística. Já vinha ficando meio triste com a cena do rock, que estava morrendo, já não tinha muito show para fazer. A coisa foi dando uma desmotivada e a gente colocou um ponto final no projeto. Foi meio triste, porque foi praticamente um casamento. Fiquei num luto por um tempo. E quem me deu uma revigorada foi um amigo, o Lucas Paz, que me convidou para fazer vídeos no YouTube.

g1 — Foi aí que o humor começou a querer aparecer?

Defante — Sim. Eu já tinha uma coisa meio performática na banda. Saía da bateria, falava besteira no microfone, queria que o público estivesse olhando para a gente mesmo quando não estava tocando. O Lucas percebeu isso e falou: “Você é um moleque engraçado. Não quer fazer uns vídeos de comédia comigo?”. Eu já tinha feito publicidade e propaganda e tinha experiência com audiovisual, então comecei a editar também. Me senti muito vivo com aquilo.

Diogo Defante dançando lambadão em Cuiabá — Foto: Redes sociais

g1 — E como foi o período em que você trabalhou com Felipe Neto?

Diogo Defante — Montei um projeto chamado Canal Foco, e fui parar na Paramaker, onde fui contratado para trabalhar nesse canal. Na época, tivemos uma reunião com o Felipe Neto, que era dono da Paramaker. Ficamos muito felizes porque a coisa começou a andar. Pensei: “Caraca, é possível ganhar dinheiro com uma parada artística”. Depois de um tempo, o Felipe Neto mudou um pouco a trajetória da Paramaker e, cerca de um ano e meio depois, já não estávamos mais em parceria com eles. Foi quando decidi fazer meu próprio canal. Pensei: “Ah, quer saber? Vou fazer a minha parada, do meu jeito”.

g1 — E quando você percebeu que o Repórter Doidão poderia virar um fenômeno?

Defante — Demorou. O quadro ficou uns dois anos sem visualização nenhuma. Eu mostrava para os amigos e tinha aquela gana de fazer por fazer. Até que um corte de uma entrevista viralizou no Facebook. A galera começou a perguntar: “De onde é isso? Quem é esse cara?”. Quando chegava ao canal, já tinha uns dez, 15 vídeos de Repórter Doidão. Aí fidelizou um público. Pensei: “Vou continuar”.

g1 — E a música ficou onde nesse período?

Defante — Meu coração ficou inundado daquela novidade de outra forma de arte. Mas, se você pegar os primórdios do meu canal, tem vídeos meus tocando bateria e tentando implementar um pouco da música. Eu sempre voltava um pouquinho. Na pandemia, como não podia mais fazer o Repórter Doidão na rua, comecei a fazer lives musicais. Foi quando mostrei músicas minhas antigas, como “Jerry” e “Padeiro”, e o pessoal que já me seguia começou a falar: “Você tem que gravar isso, fazer show”.

Defante — Exatamente. Falei: “Vamos gravar essas cinco musiquinhas e ver qual é”. De repente rola show, de repente não rola. E aí fiz o primeiro trabalho, conseguimos show até no Circo Voador. Eu não acreditava que ia dar público, de verdade. Choveu muito naquele dia e pensei: “Não vai vir ninguém”. Mas fizemos praticamente para a casa lotada. Foi arrepiador. Meu pai estava assistindo. Ali eu pensei: “Funcionou”.

Diogo Defante aposta no humor e no deboche também na carreira musical. — Foto: @felipe.alberto.s

g1 — Você também passou por uma cirurgia para retirar um tumor nesta mesma época, né? Como foi esse período?

Diogo Defante — Eu tinha uma ptose palpebral adquirida. Não nasci com isso: minha pálpebra começou a cair por conta de um inchaço. Depois descobri que era um tumor benigno que estava inflamando o olho, a ponto de enfraquecer o tendão e fazer a pálpebra cair. A galera já tinha se acostumado com aquilo, porque era uma característica que eu tinha há algum tempo. Decidi operar porque a situação estava piorando. Eu estava acompanhando com o médico, e ele falou: "Daqui a pouco o tendão perde a força, então é melhor corrigir isso logo”. Depois, com a idade, a recuperação poderia ficar mais difícil. Eu falei: “Mano, vou ter que resolver isso. Vou ter que entrar na faca, não vai ter jeito”. Foi minha primeira cirurgia.

Diogo Defante no Planeta — Foto: Agência Preview/Divulgação

g1 — E o que você prioriza hoje? A música é um plano B?

Defante — Plano B, não. Eu chamo de plano A. Já está tão forte na minha vida que considero que está caminhando junto. O entretenimento, o meu programa, o Rango e esse projeto musical. Óbvio que não consigo ter uma agenda de shows tão cheia por causa do trabalho que faço de entretenimento... mas tudo está sendo feito em paralelo.

g1 — Você acha que o seu trabalho como cantor é levado a sério?

Defante — O Mamonas Assassinas me deu a consciência de que é possível fazer uma música com galhofa, com besteirol, e ainda assim ser levado a sério. Estar no mercado da música, ser convidado para programas, vender ingresso, estar em palcos grandes. Não acho que uma música precisa ter uma letra séria para ser considerada música.

g1 — E o que você quer que o público leve de um show seu?

Defante — Quero que as pessoas se divirtam. Para mim, subir no palco é tipo: “Agora eu vou brincar”. Acho que isso traz uma leveza para as pessoas. É um monte de coisa maluca para elas cantarem junto e lavarem a alma, no sentido de sair um pouco da realidade. Acho que esse é o meu objetivo.

g1 — E agora vem o Rock in Rio. É o maior show da sua carreira?

Defante — Com certeza. Com o lançamento do meu novo single, “Humanoide”, pensei em trabalhar no show uma temática meio futurista, que converse com tecnologia e inteligência artificial. A gente está trabalhando em um telão específico para isso, com uma possível invasão cibernética de um robô interagindo com o público.

Também estamos preparando figurinos para a banda, uma coisa que ainda não tivemos, mas que acho que merece. Quero um uniforme meio futurista, dedicado a essa temática. E quero fazer uma entrada triunfal de um robô humanoide. Acho que vai ser maneiro e chamar a atenção, principalmente porque muita gente talvez nem saiba que eu tenho um projeto musical ou nunca tenha ido a um show meu.

Diogo Defante — Moleque, só consigo pensar nisso. Só consigo pensar nisso, meu irmão. Hoje eu estava vendo que precisamos ter um iluminador e que ele precisa vir aos ensaios para pensarmos a luz juntos, em cima do repertório. Quero que a iluminação fique casadinha com o show.

g1 — E tem alguma atração do festival que você quer muito ver?

Diogo Defante — Eu quero ver o Foo Fighters. Muito. Vou dar meu jeito, moleque. Inclusive, vou arrastar meu pai, que não é muito do rock. Acho que vai ser engraçado viver essa experiência com ele do lado. A gente chegou a fazer cover do Foo Fighters também, na Let's Go. Tocávamos “The Pretender” e “All My Life”. Eram duas músicas que a gente tocava muito.

Diogo Defante no clipe de “Humanoide”, single que aborda a relação entre humanos e inteligência artificial. — Foto: Divulgação.

g1 — Você tem essa personalidade de experimentar e testar coisas diferentes na música, nos clipes, no palco, nos vídeos... Quando pensa em você como artista, onde quer chegar?

Diogo Defante — Não tem isso assim. É meio que só pelo prazer. O tesão está no palco e você não pensa em sonhos nesse sentido, em metas. Mas eu quero muito que mais gente goste do som. A caminhada é árdua, então ainda vão existir situações em que vamos passar por dificuldades, como não ter um público suficiente para pagar as contas desse projeto. Quero conseguir crescer mais e mais, a ponto de pelo menos a coisa se equilibrar financeiramente para eu continuar fazendo isso pelo resto da minha vida, pelo tesão de estar no palco, de fazer isso até velhinho. Então pretendo ter esse público que me acompanhe eternamente, bom, não eternamente mas até enquanto eu durar.

g1 — Mas tem aquele clichê de que ser artista é a única maneira de viver para sempre. Você não pensa assim?

Diogo Defante — É verdade. Como estou ouvindo um monte de bandas antigas, às vezes de músicos que já se foram, é muito foda pensar que os caras já morreram, mas, de alguma forma, despertaram alguma coisa criativa em mim para eu criar também. A arte é muito compartilhada. Acho isso muito foda. Realmente, é verdade, é eterno.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Richard Gere: 'People don't understand what happiness is, so they have an idea of what will make them happy, but it never does,' powerful life lesson on the real meaning of contentment, emotional health, maturity, and self-awareness
articles.summary: Explore Richard Gere's insightful quote on happiness, emotional maturity, and self-awareness. Discover the true meaning of contentment beyond material possessions and societal expectations.
articles.body: Richard Gere is one of the Hollywood stars whose passion and dedication towards his craft cannot be defined in words. The 77-year-old Hollywood icon started his journey as a musician in high school and played several instruments. After completing high school, he went to college but left it after two years to pursue acting. His journey from Broadway to Hollywood today is treated as a blueprint by several aspiring stars. Over the years, he has portrayed some of Hollywood's most memorable characters. He has been appreciated for every on-screen persona, but his opinions on happiness reveal a more thoughtful aspect of his personality. Today's quote shows a different side of Gere and highlights true emotional maturity.Today's quote of the day by Richard Gere reads, "People don't understand what happiness is, so they have an idea of what will make them happy, but it never does".What does the quote by Richard Gere mean?While talking to The Guardian in an old interview from 2022, Richard Gere talked about how pursuing happiness can feel confusing at some points in life. It's been over two decades since he shared these words of wisdom, but this observation remains relevant even today.Gere's words cast a shadow on the very idea that has been ruling society for ages: personal happiness can be brought by money, success, relationships or possessions. People chase after what they think will make them happy, but in reality they are not happy when they get it because happiness does not lie in these external things. It takes a lot of work on the inside to truly understand what happiness is and how we can attain it; it is not simply about getting what you want.Why does Richard Gere's quote still matter today?The image of happiness has changed today, and thus, it is now difficult to differentiate between appearing happy and truly feeling joy. The quote reminds us that fulfilment doesn’t come from doing something to maintain an image. It might make one feel good, but can only offer short-lived happiness, as true contentment comes from within. It is rooted in emotional depth and maturity, not in quick fixes. Gere’s quote holds relevance today because people are still measuring success on the grounds of materialist gains.Gere's comment influences people to stop and review whether the things they are achieving actually make them happy or merely reflect what they have been taught to value.Early life of Richard GereHe was born on August 31, 1949, in Philadelphia and grew up in New York. He studied philosophy at the University of Massachusetts Amherst on a gymnastics scholarship but left college to pursue acting. He began his professional career in theatre before moving into film. Gere began appearing in Hollywood films in the mid-1970s.How Richard Gere became a Hollywood starGere gained wider attention with films including ‘Days of Heaven’ and ‘American Gigolo’. He was famous for ‘An Officer and a Gentleman’ and the 1990 romantic comedy ‘Pretty Woman’, which established him as one of Hollywood’s leading stars. He later earned a Golden Globe for his performance as Billy Flynn in ‘Chicago’ and continued working across film and television.What is Richard Gere doing now?Gere has maintained a balance in acting with humanitarian work. He has been involved in human-rights and health-related causes for decades and has served as chairman of the International Campaign for Tibet. His recent film work includes ‘Longing’, while ‘Oh, Canada’ has also been among his recent projects.More than two decades after Gere shared his thoughts on happiness, the idea behind his words remains simple: achieving what we think we want does not necessarily tell us what will make us fulfilled.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh': Who was Neem Karoli Baba, the guru whose teachings influenced Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg and Julia Roberts
articles.summary: Vishal Chaturvedi's 'Hanuman Ansh' brings the life and spiritual journey of Neem Karoli Baba to the big screen. The devotional drama is inspired by th.
articles.body: Vishal Chaturvedi's 'Hanuman Ansh' brings the life and spiritual journey of Neem Karoli Baba to the big screen. The devotional drama is inspired by the life of the spiritual teacher, who was widely known as Maharaj-ji. Vishal Chaturvedi has written and directed the film.Chandan Anand and Shobhinav Satyaa play the lead roles in the movie. The ensemble cast also includes Nikhil Dubey, Udaysinh Rajput, Purnima Tiwari and Mannish Chaudhary. Vishal Chaturvedi, who earlier worked as a doctor, has also penned the screenplay and dialogues.Who was Neem Karoli Baba?Neem Karoli Baba was a Hindu spiritual teacher and devoted follower of Lord Hanuman. He was born as Lakshman Narayan Sharma around 1900 in Akbarpur village in Uttar Pradesh. He passed away on September 11, 1973, in Vrindavan.Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand remains closely associated with his life and teachings. The location became an important spiritual centre for his followers. His influence eventually extended beyond India through devotees who carried his message to other parts of the world.Several extraordinary stories have been associated with Neem Karoli Baba over the years. Many of these accounts were narrated by his followers. His life also did not follow the traditional path expected of a religious teacher.He spent years travelling as a sadhu before eventually returning to family life. Love, compassion, devotion and selfless service formed the foundation of his teachings.Ram Dass introduced his teachings to the WestAs reported by Indian Express, one of Neem Karoli Baba's most prominent followers was American spiritual teacher Ram Dass. Born Richard Alpert, he had worked as a Harvard psychologist before travelling to India.His meeting with Neem Karoli Baba became a major turning point in his life. Ram Dass later documented his spiritual experiences in the book 'Be Here Now'.The book played a significant role in introducing Neem Karoli Baba's teachings to a wider Western audience. It also helped establish the spiritual teacher's influence among readers outside India.Why Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg visited Kainchi DhamNeem Karoli Baba's name has also been associated with some of the world's most prominent technology figures. Apple's co-founder Steve Jobs travelled to India during the 1970s and visited Kainchi Dham.Reportedly, Neem Karoli Baba had already passed away by the time Steve Jobs reached the ashram. However, the journey remained an important experience for Steve Jobs. In a 1985 interview with Playboy, Steve Jobs discussed how his time in India affected his perspective.Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg alsKarolio visited Kainchi Dham. His trip came during a difficult period for Facebook. The visit reportedly helped him reconnect with the company's original purpose.Julia Roberts and her connection with Neem Karoli BabaHollywood actor Julia Roberts has also spoken about her interest in Neem Karoli Baba. Her connection began after she came across his photograph.At that point, Julia Roberts knew very little about the spiritual teacher. Yet she said she felt strongly drawn towards his image. She later spoke about the experience while appearing in an interview with George Stephanopoulos on 'Good Morning America'.Her account further contributed to the growing global interest in Neem Karoli Baba. What is 'Hanuman Ansh' about?'Hanuman Ansh' focuses on the early life and spiritual transformation of Lakshman Das. The character is introduced as a 13-year-old boy from Braj who loses his mother.Following the tragedy, Lakshman leaves his hometown. He begins searching for divine love and a deeper spiritual connection with Lord Rama through devotion to Hanuman.His journey takes him through temples, forests, rivers and villages. As he grows older, Lakshman moves away from material possessions and conventional religious structures. He instead finds spiritual fulfilment through meditation, nature and selfless service.A significant episode in the story involves Lakshman's encounter with a railway train. The incident eventually becomes linked to the creation of the railway station that came to be known as Neem Karori.Through Lakshman Das's journey, 'Hanuman Ansh' attempts to portray the spiritual path that eventually shaped Neem Karoli Baba. articles.body: The much-awaited sequel to Prabhas starrer 'Kalki 2898 AD' has completed only a brief shooting schedule so far. Director Nag Ashwin has confirmed that the team has filmed for around 10 days. The next major schedule will begin once Prabhas becomes available.The sequel follows the success of 'Kalki 2898 AD', which released in theatres in 2024. The film featured Prabhas, Amitabh Bachchan, Kamal Haasan and Deepika Padukone in key roles. The filmmaker was speaking at the pre-release event of Dulquer Salmaan's 'I’m Game' when he discussed the sequel.As quoted by Pinkvilla, the director said, “The planets have aligned and even taken a round. So, we will begin shooting again when they align and can take another round. Not much. We shot for only about 10 days. Once Prabhas garu is free, we will shoot in a long stretch.”Amitabh Bachchan shares set picturesEarlier this year, Amitabh Bachchan had provided a glimpse of his work on the sequel. articles.body: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and actor Pawan Kalyan turned 55 on Wednesday. His birthday prompted greetings from political leaders, colleagues and family members.Prime Minister Narendra Modi was among those who wished Pawan Kalyan. He highlighted the actor-politician's contribution to the NDA government in Andhra Pradesh. Narendra Modi also praised his role in advancing the alliance's governance agenda."Birthday greetings to Shri Pawan Kalyan Garu. He is widely respected among the people and is at the forefront of adding momentum to the good governance agenda of the NDA in Andhra Pradesh. May he be blessed with a long and healthy life in service of society," PM Modi wrote.Pawan Kalyan responds to Narendra ModiPawan Kalyan responded to the Prime Minister's birthday message on X. Your affection and encouragement are deeply humbling and strengthen my resolve to serve the people of Andhra Pradesh with greater commitment. Carrying the dreams and aspirations of 1.4 billion Indians, your unwavering commitment towards building a Viksit Bharat continues to inspire the Nations aspirations. Under your visionary leadership and through the collective strength of the NDA, we shall continue working with determination for good governance, development, and the welfare of our people.I seek your continued blessings and guidance as I carry forward my responsibilities in the service of Andhra Pradesh and Bharat. @PMOIndia."Sujeeth recalls admiring Pawan KalyanFilmmaker Sujeeth shared an emotional birthday message for Pawan Kalyan. She took to Instagram to celebrate his birthday and reflected on the affection he receives from people."Celebrating you today. You are in so many hearts, thoughts and prayers - a beautiful reflection of how many lives you have touched and how much you have given to others. articles.title: Mahesh Babu’s son Gautam Ghattamaneni gives Yash’s ‘Toxic’ just 0.5 stars, Lokesh Kanagaraj’s ‘DC’ four stars while ‘Pokiri’ and ‘Nenokkadine’ score 5 on popular tracking website
articles.summary: Mahesh Babu’s son Gautam Ghattamaneni, has sparked discussion among movie fans after his ratings on Letterboxd, a popular social network and discovery.
articles.body: Mahesh Babu’s son Gautam Ghattamaneni, has sparked discussion among movie fans after his ratings on Letterboxd, a popular social network and discovery platform for film lovers, drew attention online. His scores for several films, including his father’s movies and Yash’s recently released 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups,' have particularly caught the eye of Telugu cinema fans.Gautam Ghattamaneni’s Letterboxd movie ratingsGautam Ghattamaneni’s Letterboxd profile suggests that he has watched films across multiple languages and industries, with more than 400 titles reportedly listed on his account. Interestingly, his ratings suggest that he does not automatically favour films featuring his father, Mahesh Babu. While some of the actor’s movies have received high scores from Gautam, others have been rated considerably lower. Mahesh Babu-starrers 'Pokiri' and 'Nenokkadine' are among his highest-rated films, with both receiving five stars. 'Athadu' has been rated 4.5 stars, while 'Okkadu' and 'Murari' received four stars each.On the other hand, 'Brahmotsavam' received just one star, while 'Nijam' and 'Vamsi' were given two stars each.Yash’s ‘Toxic’ gets just half a starYash’s 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' appears to have received one of Gautam’s lowest ratings. The Geetu Mohandas directorial was reportedly given just 0.5 stars out of five on his Letterboxd profile. The South Cinemaa Twitter account highlighted the rating while sharing several other scores attributed to Gautam’s profile.The post read, “#GautamGhattamaneni’s Letterboxd ratings are going viral especially his ½ for #Toxic”It also listed his ratings for films including 'Pokiri', 'Nenokkadine', 'Athadu', 'Okkadu', 'Murari', 'Brahmotsavam', 'Sholay', 'Baahubali 2', 'Pelli Choopulu', 'Sita Ramam', 'Liger' and 'Kalki 2898 AD'.The ratings prompted some fans to praise Gautam for what they viewed as an independent approach to cinema, particularly given his connection to one of Telugu cinema’s biggest stars.One fan wrote that the ratings suggested Gautam was “judging films independently rather than simply favoring his father’s work.”Gautam gives Lokesh Kanagaraj’s ‘DC’ four starsGautam has also reportedly rated Lokesh Kanagaraj’s 'DC' four stars on Letterboxd. His profile features films from a wide range of industries and genres, reflecting his interest in both Indian and international cinema. Among the films reportedly given five stars are Sholay, Project Hail Mary, Knives Out and Jersey. The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day have received 4.5 stars. Meanwhile, Liger reportedly received the same 0.5-star rating as Toxic, while Prabhas’ Kalki 2898 AD was given 2.5 stars.Some of Gautam Ghattamaneni’s ratings reportedly disappearThere also appears to have been a change in Gautam’s Letterboxd activity, with some ratings that had previously been discussed online reportedly no longer visible on his profile. His ratings for Toxic, Ravi Teja’s Irumudi and Suriya’s Viswanath and Sons appear to have been removed. It is unclear when or why the ratings disappeared.‘Toxic’ continues its box-office runDespite receiving mixed reactions, Yash’s 'Toxic' continues to maintain a steady presence at the box office. According to Sacnilk, the film earned an estimated Rs. 8.20 crore net in India on Day 7 from 12,894 shows. The Tuesday collection was reportedly 7.2% higher than its Day 6 India net collection of Rs. 7.65 crore. With the latest figures, 'Toxic' has reportedly collected Rs. 229.95 crore net in India. articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh' had a shaky start at ticket counters, but the small-budget biopic on Neem Karoli Baba has since turned into one of the year's biggest box office surprises. Nearly a month after its release, the film continues to add solid numbers, even outperforming bigger releases on comparable days. Here's a complete breakdown of how 'Hanuman Ansh' fared on Day 26.'Hanuman Ansh' box office collection Day 26Starting with a modest Day 1 total of around Rs 10 lakh, 'Hanuman Ansh' managed only about Rs 1.48 crore across its opening fortnight. The real shift came on Day 17, when the film suddenly jumped to Rs 2.20 crore in a single day, powered by strong word-of-mouth publicity and favourable reactions online. That surge carried into week three, which alone contributed a hefty Rs 10.40 crore to the total collection.As per data tracked by Sacnilk, the film registered a 54.56 percent jump over its Monday numbers on Day 26, pulling in Rs 8.50 crore from 7,008 shows nationwide.Notably, this single-day figure surpasses the Day 7 collection of Yash-starrer 'Toxic: A Fairytale for Grown Ups', directed by Geetu Mohandas, which had earned Rs 7.85 crore on its seventh day.With this latest addition, 'Hanuman Ansh' has pushed its overall India gross to Rs 63.82 crore, while its India net collection now stands at Rs 54.13 crore.Day-wise and week-wise breakdownWeek 1: Rs 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs 0.4 croreWeek 3: Rs 10.40 croreDay 22: Rs 6.25 croreDay 23: Rs 9.25 croreDay 24: Rs 12.75 croreDay 25: Rs 5.15 croreDay 26: Rs 8.50 croreTotal Net: Rs 54.13 croreMore about 'Hanuman Ansh'Helmed by writer-director Vishal Chaturvedi, 'Hanuman Ansh' traces the life story of revered spiritual figure Neem Karoli Baba, widely known as Maharaj-ji.The film's official synopsis reads, "A grieving boy seeks God to meet his departed mother, and in finding the divine, learns to serve humanity with miracles of love, food and silent blessings, becoming Hanuman Ansh, Neem Karoli Baba."Made on a reported budget of just Rs 1.75 to 2 crore, the film hit theatres on August 7, 2026. It initially clashed with 'Ohh My Dog' and 'Aryabhatta Ka Zero', before facing 'Awarapan 2' and 'Batwara 1947'.
